curriculum.lesson_evidence: When a new item is faulty, the general consumer idea in Australia is that you go back to the seller, not only to the manufacturer, and you can ask for a repair, replacement or refund. This lesson does not quote a section number of the Australian Consumer Law. Rules change in their detail, so a parent checks the current official advice before a real complaint. Proof helps: the receipt, the date, and a clear description of the fault. “I changed my mind” is a different situation from “the zip failed on day two”.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A jumper is the wrong colour and you simply prefer blue. Is that the same as a split zip? What should you say at the counter?

FEEDBACK
No. A colour preference is a change of mind. The shop may help as a courtesy, but it is not the same as a faulty zip. Say what is actually true: you prefer a different colour. Do not pretend it broke.

WATCH FOR
Inventing a statute number or threatening a fine you cannot explain. A clear, true description of the fault is the skill.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
